title: Canary prefetch mismatch — P95 spike postmortem
content:
Summary:
During a staged canary rollout of runtime optimization v2.14 on 2025-01-12 we observed a sustained P95 latency regression (service-wide) that correlated with canary traffic. The canary was rolled back within 22 minutes; this document captures the investigation, root cause, immediate mitigations, and follow-ups.

Impact:
- P95 generation latency increased from baseline ~120ms to ~420ms for affected canaries; P99 showed smaller relative increase but remained noisy.
- Affected: ~12% of requests routed to canary pools (regional canaries in us-west1).
- No increased error-rate (5xx) was observed, but tail latency caused timeouts in a small number of downstream consumer jobs.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-01-12 15:04 — Canary rollout initiated (10% traffic to canaries, staggered by region).
- 2025-01-12 15:18 — Automated canary metrics check flagged P95 > alarm threshold in us-west1. Pager triggered.
- 2025-01-12 15:22 — On-call (Aisha) ran smoke queries against canary; observed high-latency tail in generation traces.
- 2025-01-12 15:31 — Canary traffic cut back to 0% (rollback) while investigation continued.
- 2025-01-12 16:05 — Rollback completed; observed P95 returning to baseline by ~16:12.

Investigation notes:
Initial hypotheses: model weight corruption, tokenization mismatch, kernel selection regression, increased device memory pressure.
What we observed:
- Traces showed long stalls inside the model forward loop centered around KV cache prefetch calls (prefetch_kv_cache()). The stalls appeared as 30–150ms pauses before subsequent attention ops.
- Device resident memory rose ~15% on canary GPUs under nominal QPS relative to control pool, with transient spikes aligned to the stalls.
- GPU driver logs contained sporadic "context-switch wait" and "memory reclaim" entries contemporaneous with the stalls.
- Canary instrumentation tags were missing for several requests (metric export instrumentation bug in the new runtime), so some internal metrics were underpopulated which initially masked the memory-pressure signal.
- No tokenization differences or weight checksum mismatches were found. Model binaries matched expected checksums.

Root cause (summary):
An optimization (prefetch-to-kv-cache) intended to overlap KV fetches with compute introduced a subtle scheduling dependency when combined with our continuous batching codepath. Under typical batch-size/sequence-length skew seen during the canary workload, the optimization caused the runtime to issue asynchronous prefetches that increased transient device-resident allocations. On some GPUs (older driver revision present in the canary pool), this triggered driver-level memory reclaim/context switching behavior, causing synchronous stalls visible as P95 spikes. Additionally, a logging/metrics change in the same release suppressed a tag used by our memory telemetry aggregator, delaying detection of rising device memory as the primary signal.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- 15:31 — Traffic to canaries set to 0% (rollback).
- 15:34 — Disabled prefetch-to-kv-cache feature flag cluster-wide for the release branch using the rollout control plane.
- 15:45 — Temporarily enabled an audio- (not relevant) sorry: enabled additional smoke checks that pull device-resident memory and GPU driver stall counts and export them to the SRE dashboard for postmortem.
- 16:05 — Validated metrics returned to baseline after rollback and feature-flag disable.

Why automated canary checks didn't stop rollout earlier:
- Our canary gating evaluates error-rate, median latency and a small set of distribution checks. The P95-focused alarm was present but the metric emitter for device-resident memory had a missing instrumentation tag due to a minor refactor in the release, so the automated guard did not catch the growing memory signal.

Corrective actions (short term):
1) Patch to runtime v2.14.1 — revert prefetch-to-kv-cache by default; add guard rails to avoid issuing prefetch when predicted device-resident memory would exceed threshold. Owner: Jared Kim — ETA 2025-01-15.
2) Restore missing metric tag and backfill a short window of aggregated device memory stats to SLO dashboards. Owner: Marina Lopez — ETA 2025-01-14.
3) Update canary gating to include P95 and device-resident memory checks before promotion to wider rollout. Owner: eng-sre team — ETA 2025-01-18.
4) Add a targeted synthetic canary workload that simulates sequence-length skew and memory-pressure patterns to catch prefetch-related regressions. Owner: Drew O'Neal — ETA 2025-01-22.
5) Add GPU driver stall counter alert (threshold to be determined after analysis). Owner: Ravi Singh — ETA 2025-01-20.

Corrective actions (longer term):
- Introduce canary pool driver-version parity gating: don't include GPUs with older drivers in sensitive rollouts by default.
- Make prefetch-to-kv-cache opt-in per-model with safety checks in the runtime that can fallback to conservative fetch behavior when memory pressure is detected.
- Add a canary experiment to validate instrumentation after release steps (small traffic test that validates all metric tags are present).

Runbook draft (quick steps for on-call):
1) If P95 rises > 2x baseline in canary region and device memory metric missing/unavailable: cut traffic to canary and pause rollout.
2) Check device-resident-memory time-series and GPU driver stall counters for alignment with latency spikes.
3) If memory pressure/stalls present: disable prefetch-to-kv-cache via feature flag and observe.
4) If rollout can't be easily rolled back: scale canary pool down to single machine and isolate by model/version to reduce cross-tenant noise.
5) Open postmortem ticket, tag eng-sre and runtime teams, and notify product and solutions-eng owners listed in the release note.

Postmortem notes and learnings:
- Small instrumentation regressions can materially delay detection of root causes; instrumentation is as critical as the code change.
- Optimizations that change allocation timing (not just totals) can interact badly with hardware/software combos; test for memory-alloc timing as well as steady-state memory.
- Canary gating must include distributional tail metrics (P95/P99) and resource-level signals (device memory, driver stalls) for inference workloads.

Action items (with owners & due dates):
- Runtime patch (revert prefetch default + guard): Jared Kim — 2025-01-15.
- Instrumentation tag fix + backfill: Marina Lopez — 2025-01-14.
- Canopy synthetic workload creation: Drew O'Neal — 2025-01-22.
- Update canary gating rules: eng-sre team (Ravi Singh lead) — 2025-01-18.
- Driver-parity policy proposal: eng-sre + platform-eng — 2025-02-01.

Appendix (useful commands & quick links):
- Query device memory (prod): influxql "SELECT mean("gpu_mem_resident") FROM metrics WHERE region='us-west1' AND pool='canary' AND time > now() - 1h"
- GPU driver logs path: /var/log/nvidia-driver.log on canary nodes
- Rollback CLI: redwoodctl rollout promote --target=stable --from=canary --dry-run=false
- Canary health dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/board/canary-health

Notes on evidence collection: preserved core dumps and driver logs from two affected nodes (node-uw1-canary-07, node-uw1-canary-03) in S3 bucket s3://redwood-incidents/2025-01-12-prefetch-canary/ for runtime team.

Owner for postmortem follow-up: Aisha Patel (eng-sre).

Status: this doc is a draft postmortem; short-term fixes deployed 2025-01-14; long-term items in progress.
